newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B share indices end up on A share gains.
newsitem.headline: China's B share indices end up on A share gains.

text.p: China's foreign currency B share indices closer higher on Friday although trading was slow with most overseas buyers keeping to the sidelines, awaiting the release of 1996 company results, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index edged up 0.218 points or 0.30 percent to 73.494 points on volume of 15.07 million shares worth $8.26 million.
Shanghai's A index rose 15.860 points or 1.21 percent to 1,321.586 points on turnover of 12.2 billion yuan.
Trading was not active before the release of company results, which are due by an April 30 deadline, brokers said.
However, the strong A share performance encouraged domestic investors in the B share market, although institutions remained sidelined, brokers said.
"Most investors are taking a wait-and-see attitude during the company report season," one broker said.
"But market sentiment is strong, with investors confident there are more opportunities to make money on the stock markets this year due to improved fundamentals," one broker said.
Real estate developer Shanghai Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development was the star in domestic buying, up $0.014 or 3.05 percent to $0.472 on volume of 443,000 shares.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products was the most actively traded stock on expectations of good results, gaining $0.020 or 2.70 percent to $0.760 on volume of 1.8 million shares.
Shenzhen's B share index inched up 0.07 points or 0.04 percent to 161.27 on turnover of HK$58.8 million, compared with Thursday's HK$44.1 million.
On the B share market, the biggest gainer was Shenzhen Great Ocean Shipping Co Ltd, up HK$0.11 or 2.95 percent to HK$3.84.
The Shanghai A share index closed at its highest level since May 5, 1993 on bullish sentiment, but was off its intraday high of 1,331.130 points on profit-taking just before the close.
The SSE30 index put on 55.467 points or 1.60 percent to end at 3,523.073 points.
Shanghai Oriental Pearl saw heavy buying on expectations of a good bonus issue plan, jumping 2.05 yuan or 10.00 percent to 22.55 yuan on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Shenzhen's A index gained 5.65 points or 1.23 percent to 464.02 on turnover of 12.4 billion yuan against 7.4 billion yuan.
